thread.title: Correction: Mid-Day Update: Dow Breaks Record As Italy Concedes and ISM Sets 21-Year High

author: MT Newswires
title: Correction: Mid-Day Update: Dow Breaks Record As Italy Concedes and ISM Sets 21-Year High
text:
Shutterstock photo (Correction to ISM high in headline, first and fourth paragraphs. The ISM non-manufacturing index of 61.6 in September was the highest since 1997, not 2005. A correct version follows)
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was higher for a fifth straight day after Italy's concession to lower its budget deficit target to 2.0% triggered a relief rally across Europe and the US. Led higher by a larger-than-expected increase in private payrolls and 21-year high in a leading measure of the services sector of the economy, the blue chip index set another record high on outsized gains in Apple ( AAPL ) Boeing ( BA ) and Caterpillar ( CAT ).
The services sector came into focus Wednesday with both the ADP private payroll data, purchasing managers and Institute for Supply Management indices. Service-providing industries created 184,000 new jobs in September, surpassing a modest 46,000 gain in the goods-producing sector for a total of 230,000 new jobs in the private sector. This beat expectations for a 179,000 gain and followed an upwardly revised 168,000 increase in August.
The final September PMI for services was down slightly from August, but a revision to 53.5 from the preliminary 52.9 was still above Wall Street's expectations.
A comparable index from the ISM, however, rose to its highest level since 1997 of 61.6 from 58.5 in August, comfortably above the consensus estimate for a slight drop to 58.0.
The reaction across Wall Street extinguished any lingering safe-haven bid, driving the Dow to its all-time high and the yield on the 30-year Treasury bond to its highest level in three years. The benchmark yield is up 7 basis points from Tuesday, followed by a 6-basis-point spike in the 10-year yield. Additionally, gold is down $4 and utility stocks are one of only two sectors of the S&P 500 trading negatively.
European stocks were also in the plus column after Rome yielded to pressure from the European Commission to lower its deficit/GDP target to 2.0% in 2021 from 2.4%. Italy's FTSE-MIB closed higher for the first time in six days, but returned most of its intra-day gains once investors digested the new specifications of the budget, namely an escape clause in which Rome can maintain a 2.4% deficit/GDP target if GDP growth disappoints. Additionally, the government can continue to keep its current 2.4% target in 2019, lowering it to just 2.2% in 2020.
Consequently, the euro returned its early gains to trade lower against the dollar for a sixth straight day, and Italian bonds resumed their sell-off.
Crude oil was up $0.33 to $75.48 per barrel. Natural gas was up $0.08 to $3.25 per 1 million BTU. Gold was down $4.00 to $1,203.00 an ounce, while silver was up $0.02 to $14.71 an ounce. Copper was up $0.008 to $2.81 per pound.
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was up 0.50% to $15.95 with the United States Natural Gas Fund up 2.83% to $26.85. Amongst precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF were down 0.26% to 18.94 while SPDR Gold Shares were down 0.31% to $113.53. The iShares Silver Trust was up 0.15% to $13.81.
